question: Under 5% reading noise, does (1) a sound stop rule (claim ID only when no start-state-distinct rival fits the fused trace with up to B_max flips, not merely at the least SAT budget) remove the least-B WRONG, and (2) an upward-doubling least-B probe (B = 0, 1, 2, 4, ... capped at B_max, then bisection inside the last bracket) avoid the capped B_max-first probe that left A11_r3 IDU on 9 of 10 noisy 12-state cases?
motivation: Study 036 (Observed): the majority of 3 reads cut the truth's base flips from 13-20 to 0-5, but on 9 of 10 A11_r3 IDU noisy12 cases the first bisection probe at B = B_max = 6 hit the 9.5 s cap. On noisy_scale8 10210002 A11_r3 and A11_r3_up stopped ID at least B 1 while the truth needed 2 flips on the fused trace; the model matched the truth's future from the final state but not from the start state (label9 WRONG). A11_r5 (B_max 2) had the best noisy12 result (ID 4/12; +0.33 [0.08,0.58] over A10, reported, not gated). GQB11: A11_r3_up 10.513 s > 10.5 s. Inferred: a least-B ID is not sound under noise, and probing the largest budget first is the expensive query

hypotheses.H1_sound: A12 arms give WRONG 0 on every clean and within-budget noisy case, including the 036 failure pattern (replayed as an Exact unit test on the sealed 036 trace of noisy_scale8 10210002)

hypotheses.H3_r5: A12_r5 keeps the A11_r5 gain with the sound stop: ID + IDF(A12_r5, noisy12) >= 5/12
hypotheses.H4_cap: a lower solver timer (9.0 s) keeps every query <= 10.5 s

arms.A12_r5: new file brute/scalesearch12.py: A11 (frozen scalesearch11) logic with r = 5 majority reads, B_max(5) = 2, two changes. (1) Sound stop: after the least-B search returns a model M at budget b, run one confirmation query at B_max asking for a machine with <= N states, <= B_max flips on the fused trace, that differs from M from the START state on some word of length <= the declared bound; SAT -> execute the separating word (as a rival pair) and continue; UNSAT -> ID; capped -> IDU. (2) Least-B probe order: B = 0, 1, 2, 4, ... up to B_max, stopping at the first SAT, then bisection inside the last UNSAT/SAT bracket
